page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is a graphics-intensive server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1880 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 95679.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16623.0, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 3980.77 GB/sec, though larger uncached read and write operations drop to average tiers at 118.74 GB/sec and 60.94 GB/sec respectively. The instance demonstrates excellent capabilities in database operations, achieving 62.3 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

The single NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for small and medium language model inference, processing prompts at 2270.07 tokens per second and generating text at 53.96 tokens per second for the 7B model. However, a significant performance tradeoff is observed with larger models; while prompt processing for a 70B model remains strong, text generation speed drops to a weak 2.71 tokens per second, indicating VRAM and compute limitations for large-scale LLM execution.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g6.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density by bundling dedicated AMD EPYC compute, local NVMe storage, and a mid-range Ada Lovelace GPU. This configuration avoids the higher costs associated with multi-GPU or high-VRAM systems while delivering strong performance for graphics rendering, ray tracing, medium-scale machine learning inference, database operations, and software compilation.
